title: Difficulty level in my game?
author: johnesco
selftext:
I've gotten pretty good at the driving game I vibe coded :)   
  
However I see many others struggle with it, and yet others who find it way too easy.

So I've added "Easy - Medium - Hard" modes, but wondering how different to make them?

Currently I plan to make "hard" so difficult that I can't even make it to first place. My thought process here is that SOMEONE will want the difficulty level. Thoughts?

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body:
best would be 5 options, but that is usually intimidating for people. so: easy -> someone who isnt good at video games (you know someone, maybe some girlfriend who never plays or a 12 year olf or smth) can manage, normal = normal dude who plays a bit of games has mild struggles, hard = you have to try, even if you are experienced gamer, but you shouldnt try to break them. the hard setting you describe is more like a 4th "hell" setting or smth.

a wise man on youtube once said: always remember that youre game is 5x more difficult for others because they dont have houndreds of hours developing it in them.

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body: So far I've tried to keep it where "Easy" I can make lots of mistakes and win, "Medium" I can't go off road much, and "Hard" I can beat it but have to play nearly perfectly to get 1st place. The reason I haven't considered more than 3 is because I also give them the choice of how many racers and civilian traffic there is, that quickly stacks the amount possibilities to test. But I would consider locking in the amount of competition and traffic, and then tuning up to 5 difficulty levels. Thanks for the feedback, will chew on this idea quite a bit.

comments.author: KidLink4
comments.body: Don't look at it as "how well can I/a player place". Look to the real world - what makes drivers actually better than others? Have your difficulty tied to actual driving techniques - higher difficulties will take better driving lines, are  less prone to oversteering, have better traction control, etc.

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body:
Each driver has a motivation in a finite-state-machine style. Either "passing" or "blocking". As a solid rule they are not given a speed or acceleration advantage or handicap. It's all down to how they race. 

One thing I've been doing is I have a mode where I race side by side with the CPU I hit a button to freeze the state, then we go over "why did the CPU make this driving choice?". An example of something I discovered is that it was predicting too far ahead and any traffic would make it slow down, leading to a "cautious vs aggressive" style. This is being split into "personalities" like the ghosts in pac man.

replies.author: KidLink4
replies.body:
This ls really unique. It's giving Midnight Club - I don't know if you're old enough to remember those games but they were the absolute shit. 

That said, I don't know if it really works in isolation. It's hard to tell without actually playing your game, but I imagine that if you don't have a solid foundation in place, your aggression tuning turns into how likely is the bot to run you off the road. Also, if you have no speed variance, where's the motivation to upgrade your own vehicle (Doesn't apply if you don't have an upgrade system)? 

If you baseline with traditional levers, such as braking at the right time, coming out of turns without wheelspin, etc. then layer your personality machine on top of it, this could be my new main racing game, not even joking.

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body: I literally have been playing video games since 1979 and I'm keeping it simple in a 2D retro-ish game. I'll post updates here once it's more fleshed out.

replies.author: KidLink4
replies.body: I didn't mean that offensively, I hope it didn't come off that way. I genuinely just wasn't sure people would know what Midnight Club was.

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body: Oh, no, I'm honored to get to talk about how long I've been at this. This is the first big project I've done so I'm keeping it simple though, it's just a [2D racer](http://vibecodesgames.itch.io/pavement/)
